streams.problem: წყლის ხარისხის ოპერატორებს შეიძლება სჭირდებოდეთ ლაბორატორიული ნიმუშებისა და უწყვეტი სენსორული telemetry-ის დროული, აუდიტირებადი შეჯერება; საქართველოში არსებული მონიტორინგის ქსელი და ლაბორატორიული კონტროლი არ უნდა ჩაითვალოს არარსებულად.
streams.research_question: შეუძლია თუ არა site-specific წესებზე, მონაცემის სიახლესა და კალიბრაციის სტატუსზე დაფუძნებულმა operator-side სისტემამ ადრე მონიშნოს ოპერაციული გადახრები ისე, რომ არ ჩაანაცვლოს ლაბორატორიული ანალიზი ან უფლებამოსილი ოპერატორის გადაწყვეტილება?
streams.human_benefit: შესაძლო ადრეული გამოვლენა და სწრაფი ოპერატორული რეაგირება სასმელი წყლის სისტემებში; საველე სარგებელი ჯერ დაუდასტურებელია.
streams.hypothesis: თუ მონაცემის ხარისხი, freshness, calibration და ობიექტის მიერ დამტკიცებული ზღვრები ცალ-ცალკე კონტროლდება, კონსერვატიული წესების ძრავა შეძლებს არასანდო მონაცემის ნორმალურ მდგომარეობად წარმოჩენის თავიდან აცილებას.
methodology: ოფიციალური წყაროების დოკუმენტური მიმოხილვა და არსებული ქართული მონიტორინგის ინფრასტრუქტურის აღწერა

შემდეგ ეტაპზე მხოლოდ უფლებამოსილი ოპერატორის მიერ ნებადართული paired sensor/laboratory მონაცემის წინასწარ რეგისტრირებული შეფასება
ლოკალური append-only SQLite event store: canonical transition replay, WAL, immediate write transaction, SHA-256 hash chain და synthetic concurrency/tamper/replay tests

Compare the locally verified AquaSignal event-chain tail hash and event count with caller-supplied trusted out-of-band checkpoint values; this comparison does not authenticate the checkpoint or prevent rollback.
Detached Ed25519 checkpoint verification over canonical UTF-8 payload bytes, with local event-chain tail matching and a caller-managed monotonic high-water state; synthetic ephemeral-key tests only.

Inventory official Georgian water-monitoring networks without combining unlike domains: NEA surface water, groundwater, marine water and the utility's raw-source/treated-network drinking-water testing are separate data streams.

Record only source-published network counts, monitoring frequency statements, parameter classes, laboratory accreditation claims and whether sample-level records/data dictionaries are publicly accessible; do not infer station-level frequency from a general news statement.

Before any ingestion, require an authorized data dictionary covering station ID/coordinates, sample timestamp, water matrix, analyte, result, units, method, LOD/LOQ, lab, accreditation, QA/QC flags, applicable standard, approved site Water Safety Plan limit, publication delay and revision history.

Evaluate any future sensor/lab pairing in shadow mode with preregistered detection delay, sensitivity, positive predictive value, false alerts per station-month, calibration drift and data completeness; require human and laboratory confirmation before operational action.

Review the 2025 Government of Georgia submission to the UNECE/WHO Protocol on Water and Health: keep NEA groundwater/surface-water monitoring separate from Food Safety Agency drinking-water compliance.

Inventory reported 2024 groundwater monitoring (72 points, 394 laboratory samples) and 2024 surface-water monitoring (331 points on 137 water bodies); preserve the report's aggregate/process evidence boundary.

Review the official 2026-11-26 NEA announcement of the 2021-2025 groundwater report and nitrate-risk field methodology; do not ingest the linked RAR archive until contents, schema and reuse terms are inspected.
Classify WIS C10/C11 as historical annual aggregates (2004-2018) and Hydromet's water-quality-points map/table as an unverified station-registry lead.
Treat 2024 E. coli non-compliance (40.3% source-reported) as a drinking-water sample statistic with missing denominator in the published table, not as population exposure.

Preserve countervailing source evidence: the UNECE/WHO government submission describes groundwater used as a drinking-water source as generally good quality, while noting isolated microbiological exceedances; do not infer a national groundwater crisis from the separate potable-network E. coli sample statistic.

Preserve the UNECE/WHO report's two E. coli reporting frames separately: narrative 2021-2022/2023/2024 and table baseline 2005/previous cycle 2019/current 2024; do not construct a continuous trend until definitions and denominators are reconciled.

Review Government of Georgia Resolution No.424 and NEA implementation notice; distinguish post-2026 wells >20 m from pre-existing and household wells, and treat the register as a prospective administrative metadata source rather than a sample-level monitoring feed.

Inspect the official MEPA GIS catalogue for groundwater station-layer metadata and distinguish a public/free catalogue classification from verified payload, download/API access, coordinate precision and reuse licence.
Keep the spatial station registry separate from sample-level analytical observations; require different adapters and schemas for station metadata, groundwater results and potable-network compliance.
Use Article 32 of Georgia's Law on Water Resources Management to distinguish NEA environmental-water monitoring data access from National Food Safety Agency drinking-water quality control.
Resolve the direct RAR archive URL linked by NEA's 2026-11-26 announcement; record the retrieval failure as an execution-environment limitation and do not infer archive contents or licence.

Review the Public Defender of Georgia's 2025 right-to-water special report as primary evidence about public-information and accountability findings; distinguish its purposive municipal visits from a nationally representative survey. Reconcile the report's disclosure recommendations with JECM's secondary analysis of NFA monitoring samples and the Government of Georgia's UNECE/WHO-submitted aggregate report; preserve the 2023 49.5% versus 44.5% discrepancy and missing sample-frame/denominator metadata. Derive a privacy-preserving, authority-owned disclosure-layer requirements proposal; no raw samples, API ingestion, field survey or operational risk scoring.

data_needs: უფლებამოსილი ოპერატორის data dictionary და პარამეტრების ერთეულები
ობიექტის დამტკიცებული Water Safety Plan და site-specific operational limits
ნებადართული ისტორიული paired sensor/laboratory ჩანაწერები, sample provenance და calibration logs
მონაცემის გამოყენებისა და ხელახალი გამოქვეყნების წერილობითი ნებართვა
Official machine-readable sample-level NEA/utility laboratory results, or a published endpoint and documented reuse terms.

Station registry and data dictionary: station identifiers, coordinates, sample timestamps, water matrix, analytes, units, analytical methods, LOD/LOQ, laboratory, accreditation scope, QA/QC and revision/correction history.
Applicable Georgian technical regulation and site-approved Water Safety Plan limits for the exact water matrix and sampling point.
Written authorization for paired sensor/laboratory data and any operational use; synthetic fixtures only until approval.
Inspect the official NEA 2021-2025 RAR archive and record internal filenames, table granularity, metadata, data dictionary and reuse terms before extracting any observations.
Obtain the denominator, geographic/system disaggregation and source microdata for the 2024 E. coli 40.3% drinking-water non-compliance statistic from the National Food Safety Agency.
Retrieve 2022-2025 NEA groundwater bulletins and monthly surface-water bulletins; verify whether tables are row-level, machine-readable and revision-stable.
Inspect Hydromet's water-quality-points table fields, station identifiers, coordinates, export format and update cadence.
Keep separate permissions and provenance for groundwater, surface-water, marine-water and potable-network datasets.

Reconcile the UNECE/WHO report's E. coli narrative (2021-2022, 2023, 2024) with table baseline/previous-cycle labels (2005, 2019, 2024), including sample denominators, sampling frame, method and coverage.
Written authorization and a privacy-reviewed, de-identified export of the post-2026 well registry, if the database is operational and access can lawfully be granted.
Clarification of registry coverage for wells drilled before 2026-09-01 and household wells, plus a data dictionary showing whether each record has field/laboratory sampling results.
For NEA catalogue record NEA122: authorised export/API URL, actual layer payload, station fields, coordinate reference system, active/inactive dates, update cadence and reuse licence.

Separate National Food Safety Agency drinking-water compliance data dictionary and denominator/geographic breakdown; do not merge potable-network records with environmental groundwater station points.
An accessible copy or official alternate transfer route for the NEA 2021–2025 RAR archive, plus internal file inventory, archive digest, report/table granularity, data dictionary and reuse terms.

Obtain an authority-approved drinking-water disclosure data dictionary and sample-frame denominators, plus the official publication/correction workflow and permitted dissemination channels; no personal or private-well records.
risks: ცრუ განგაში ან სენსორის drift-ის წყლის რეალურ ცვლილებად მიჩნევა
არასრული telemetry-ის ნორმალურ მდგომარეობად არასწორი ინტერპრეტაცია
პირადი/ოპერატორული მონაცემის საჯარო საცავში შემთხვევითი მოხვედრა
პროტოტიპის ლაბორატორიულ ან რეგულატორულ შეფასებად აღქმა
The local hash chain is tamper-evident but not signed; a privileged attacker able to rewrite and rehash the database may alter history.
The event store has no encrypted/off-host backup, retention policy, external signed checkpoint or production access-control integration.
The external checkpoint comparison authenticates neither the checkpoint nor its freshness; a stale or attacker-controlled checkpoint can validate a rolled-back database.
A signed sequence detects rollback only if the highest accepted sequence and digest are atomically held outside the SQLite database in a separately trusted, rollback-resistant service.
The prototype has no production signer, key rotation/revocation, threshold signing, remote anchor, provider retention or alerting integration.
NEA surface-water, groundwater and marine monitoring must not be conflated with drinking-water network compliance; Black Sea results cannot establish freshwater or tap-water safety.
Published network counts and general statements such as 'within norm' are not sample-level evidence, a live feed, a station-specific result or an all-time safety guarantee.
The utility's public statement about daily analyses does not expose the sampling schedule for each station, exact parameters, methods or sample records.

The 2024 E. coli non-compliance percentage is a source-reported sample statistic with no denominator or municipal breakdown in the cited table; it must not be presented as population exposure or a national unsafe-water rate.
NEA groundwater/surface-water monitoring and National Food Safety Agency potable-network compliance have different authorities, matrices, sampling frames and legal thresholds.
The new NEA 2021-2025 report is linked as a RAR archive, but its contents and machine-readable granularity have not yet been inspected.

The UNECE/WHO submission describes groundwater used as a drinking-water source as generally good quality with isolated microbiological exceedances; the 40.3% E. coli statistic concerns a separate drinking-water control sample set and must not be applied to groundwater monitoring.

The UNECE/WHO drinking-water E. coli narrative and table use different historical reference-year frames; absent sample denominators and blank urban/rural table fields prevent a defensible trend or population-risk estimate.
The legal well-registration scope excludes pre-existing wells and NEA says household wells are excluded; registry counts must not be used as total groundwater-well coverage.
Well passports request owner identity/contact data and coordinates; no personal or owner-level records may enter the public repository.

The NEA122 catalogue labels the groundwater point layer public/free but lists SQL SDE/local storage and no portal-placement URL; treating this as a directly downloadable open dataset would overstate access.
A station-location layer is not a sample-result time series; joining them without stable station IDs, water-matrix identity and provenance can create false matches.
A public dashboard could falsely reassure users if missing or stale records are displayed as safe; missing data must remain explicitly unknown and no health/safety inference may be generated.
blockers: Authorized paired sensor/laboratory data, a site data dictionary and approved Water Safety Plan limits remain unavailable under explicit reuse permission.
No field validation or independent external review has been completed.
The signed checkpoint verifier is a local software contract only; production signing-key custody and a separately administered atomic monotonic high-water service are not implemented.
Encrypted/off-host backup, remote immutable checkpoint retention, clean-host restore and production access-control integration remain unavailable.

The UNECE/WHO 2025 report confirms electronic groundwater results since 2022 and monthly surface-water bulletins, but no structured sample-level endpoint, full schema or reuse terms have yet been verified.
The NEA 2021-2025 groundwater report archive announced on 2026-11-26 is not yet extracted; its internal data granularity and licence/reuse conditions remain unknown.
The published 2024 E. coli non-compliance percentage lacks the sample denominator and municipal/system disaggregation needed for local prioritisation.

The existence of a legally required NEA hydrogeological database does not prove a public API or public reuse permission; no registry export, data dictionary or operational access policy has been verified.
The official NEA122 station-layer catalogue entry is public/free, but its actual payload, export/API path, fields, coordinate reference system and reuse licence have not been verified.
The NEA 2021–2025 groundwater report archive is linked by the Agency but its RAR contents could not be retrieved or inspected in this run.
streams.status_detail: PR #82 merged into main as a19252bb4df28e2733b6b5180c8938792c040e63. Its exact-head quality CI 45875671834 and actual CPU-thread workflow 45875671867 both succeeded. The verifier checks a strict canonical checkpoint payload, detached Ed25519 signature against caller-supplied trusted keys, expected store identity, and local event-chain hash/count; it rejects lower generations and same-sequence equivocation and marks bootstrap-only verification explicitly when no trusted high-water state is supplied. The caller must atomically persist returned state outside the SQLite rollback domain. Post-merge main quality CI 45875861427 and Pages build/deploy 45875861440 succeeded. No production signer, external high-water authority, authorized sensor/lab dataset, site-approved Water Safety Plan limits or field validation exists. A public-source Georgia monitoring inventory found existing NEA surface-water (238 locations) and groundwater (72 points) monitoring disclosures, a separate monthly Black Sea network (14 points in the July 2026 update), and a utility laboratory network described as 8 regional plus 35 service-centre labs. These are source-reported network/process facts, not sample-level data or proof of drinking-water safety. No machine-readable sample dataset or data dictionary was identified in the pages inspected; no raw result was imported. Discovery update 2026-11-27: the 2025 UNECE/WHO Georgia report states groundwater results have been available electronically since 2022, records 394 laboratory samples from 72 groundwater points in 2024, and reports 2024 surface-water sampling at 331 points on 137 water bodies. It separately reports 40.3% E. coli non-compliance in drinking-water samples for 2024, mainly microbiological, with rural small systems included; the table does not expose the denominator. NEA announced a 2021-2025 groundwater report and nitrate-risk field methodology on 2026-11-26 and linked a RAR archive that has not yet been inspected. WIS C10/C11 provide historical 2004-2018 aggregate indicators; Hydromet lists a water-quality-points map/table whose fields remain unverified. These discoveries narrow the earlier data-access blocker but do not establish a current sample-level API or reuse permission. No raw observations were imported. The UNECE/WHO submission also states that automatic groundwater stations were installed in 11 district units across 8 regional administrations during 2022-2024, 12 groundwater bulletins were published, and groundwater used as a drinking-water source was generally assessed as good quality with isolated microbiological exceedances. This countervailing source-reported evidence is recorded to avoid overstatement. The UNECE/WHO drinking-water section contains two distinct E. coli reference frames: narrative values for 2021-2022/2023/2024 and table values labelled 2005/2019/2024. They are not combined into one trend because the sample denominator and urban/rural breakdown are absent. A 2026-08-31 Government Resolution No.424 now provides a primary legal basis for a prospective well-registration source effective 2026-09-01, limited to fresh drinking-water extraction wells deeper than 20 m; pre-existing wells are outside the legal scope and NEA says household wells are excluded. The passport includes owner identity/contact data and optional field/lab result attachments, so only privacy-reviewed de-identified access can be considered. The register itself and public reuse terms remain unverified. 2026-11-27 update: MEPA's GIS catalogue exposes NEA122, a point-geometry groundwater monitoring layer classified public/free (catalogue date 2026-03-06), but its row lists SQL SDE/local storage and no portal URL; the payload and reuse licence remain unverified. NEA's 2026-06-09 notice describes automatic monitored-well stations and field data-registration/documentation procedures in Tianeti. Article 32 assigns environmental-water monitoring data to NEA and drinking-water quality state control to the National Food Safety Agency. No coordinates or sample rows were imported. 2026-11-27 AquaSignal public-information addendum: the Public Defender of Georgia's 2025 special report documents water-quality information as a major challenge after visits to five regions, 35 villages and 15 municipalities, and recommends a unified public-information platform plus supplementary channels. JECM's 2025 article is explicitly a secondary analysis of NFA monitoring data; the Government of Georgia's UNECE/WHO-submitted report reports a different 2023 broad non-compliance value (44.5% versus JECM 49.5%), with no sample-frame/denominator detail sufficient to reconcile it. This supports a public-disclosure/accessibility research question, not a claim that Georgian water is nationally unsafe. New note and structured evidence are Draft; no raw sample, household, health, personal or private-well data imported.
streams.next_step: Obtain the NEA 2021–2025 RAR archive and NEA122 layer metadata through an accessible official route; separately request from NFA and relevant utilities an approved disclosure data dictionary, 2023/2024 sample denominators and sample-frame definitions, correction/version policy and existing citizen-information channels. Do not ingest or republish sample-level data until access, licence, privacy and authority approval are verified.
success_metrics: საველე ტესტში წინასწარ განსაზღვრულ reference labels-თან შედარებული sensitivity და positive predictive value
false-alert rate და detection delay წინასწარ განსაზღვრულ baseline-თან შედარებით
ყველა სიგნალზე წყაროს, freshness-ის, calibration-ისა და წესის ვერსიის მიკვლევადობა
A valid detached Ed25519 signature, expected store identifier and exact local event-chain head are all required before checkpoint acceptance.
A checkpoint sequence below external trusted state is rejected; same-sequence different payload is rejected; identical same-sequence replay is idempotent.
No rollback-protection claim is made unless next_trusted_state is atomically persisted outside the event database in a separately trusted domain.

A source inventory must keep surface, groundwater, marine and potable-network observations distinct and identify whether sample-level provenance, method, units, QA/QC and reuse permission exist before ingestion.

Every future imported observation retains matrix, station/sample identity, collection and publication timestamps, analyte, unit, method, QA/QC, source-page provenance and reuse permission; records missing mandatory fields are blocked.
No surface-water, groundwater, marine-water or potable-network observation is merged into another matrix or evaluated against an unapproved threshold.
Any 2024 E. coli trend statement preserves the published denominator limitation and reports sample-level coverage only when the underlying counts are obtained.

streams.title: რიცხვითი სიზუსტე და რეალური CPU-thread reduction
streams.problem: პარალელურმა floating-point reduction-მა შეიძლება გააძლიეროს cancellation/ordering შეცდომები; ამავე დროს რეალური threads-ის გამოყენება ავტომატურად არ ნიშნავს wall-time აჩქარებას.
streams.research_question: რომელი partial-reduction არქიტექტურა ინარჩუნებს correctly-rounded reference შედეგს რეალურ CPU threads-ზე და რა პირობებში აქვს მას გაზომვადი შესრულების უპირატესობა?
streams.human_benefit: უფრო სანდო სამეცნიერო და საინჟინრო გამოთვლები, სადაც რიცხვითი შეცდომა ან შესრულების მცდარი მოლოდინი მნიშვნელოვან შედეგს იწვევს.
streams.hypothesis: Neumaier (sum, compensation) state-ის გაერთიანება უკეთ შეინარჩუნებს სიზუსტეს scalar partial sums-თან შედარებით, თუმცა Python ThreadPool-ის overhead შეიძლება wall-time მოგებას გააქრობდეს.
methodology: დეტერმინისტული synthetic binary64 cancellation fixture და exact-rational reference
contiguous/round-robin partition-ები, 1/2/4/8 worker-ები და naive/scalar Neumaier/compensation-state მეთოდები
ოთხი დამოუკიდებელი ARM64 benchmark batch, თითოეულში ოთხი runtime cell და თითოეულ cell-ში 48 configuration
accuracy, CPU-time/wall-time და tracemalloc ცალ-ცალკე შეფასება; CPU-time/wall-time არ განიმარტოს როგორც wall-time speedup
Native C11/OpenMP comparison of serial and 1/2/4/8-thread naive, long-double, recursive pairwise, Neumaier-state and fixed-width exact-superaccumulator reductions on two frozen cancellation layouts
One warm-up and five timed repetitions per case; record actual native thread counts, monotonic wall time, process CPU time, process peak RSS and compiler/runtime provenance

Independent MPFR 4.2.1 oracle: represent the exact signed integer in 2,624-bit precision, divide by 2^1074 exactly, then convert with MPFR_RNDN; compare bit patterns against the C converter and Python Decimal on hosted x86-64 and ARM64. The native workflow asserts pkg-config reports MPFR 4.2.1.

Deterministic full-width MPFR 4.2.1 oracle extension: 1,024 seeded signed values plus 1,044 tie-adjacent values; compare C output bitwise against MPFR_RNDN, Python integer and 1,200-digit Decimal references on hosted x86-64/ARM64.

Run actual ThreadPoolExecutor native-thread experiment on CPython 3.14.4 GIL-enabled and free-threaded builds: 2 layouts × 4 worker counts × 2 partitions × 3 reduction methods × 3 repetitions, with native thread ID validation and process CPU/wall timing.

Download the original GIL-enabled and free-threaded Actions artifact ZIPs, verify archive SHA-256 against the frozen summary, and independently recompute per-case accuracy and worker-count metric aggregates.

Second real CPU-thread run raw reports were archived as gzip/base64; workflow ZIP SHA-256 and decompressed raw-report SHA-256 were checked, then per-case accuracy and metric aggregates were recomputed by scripts/reproduce_noema005_threaded_reruns.py --check.

Third hosted x86-64 rerun (GitHub Actions 45897707859): archive both GIL-enabled and free-threaded raw reports, verify ZIP hashes against GitHub artifact metadata, verify raw-report SHA-256 and independently reproduce per-method accuracy, median speedup, CPU/wall ratio, allocation and worker-count aggregates.

Independently compare matching raw JSON cases across separate KVM runs using the same source SHA and recorded host/cgroup provenance; report per-worker timing variation rather than pooling runs into a portable speedup.
Audit paired per-repetition process-CPU and monotonic wall-time samples; compare process CPU/wall ratios with the recorded effective cgroup CPU set, not only with requested OpenMP worker counts.
Keep correctness, timing validity, and resident-memory bandwidth as separate evidence questions; use a fail-closed rule for timing claims when resource provenance is inconsistent.

streams.status_detail: PR #81 merged into main as a69c3f29a7dec0f25f3a30c60f2d9f4d671807c7. Its exact-head quality CI 45872887590 and actual CPU-thread workflow 45872887552 both succeeded. The archived second raw-report set from workflow 45867519546 was rechecked: archive hashes and decompressed report hashes matched the frozen metadata, and scripts/reproduce_noema005_threaded_reruns.py --check reproduced all per-case accuracy counts and aggregate ranges. In that archived run, Neumaier-state median speedup was 0.7744x (range 0.7225–0.7935) with GIL and 1.0181x (range 0.7023–1.135) on free-threaded CPython; the prior free-threaded run was 0.9519x. The crossing of 1.0 is run-to-run variability, not evidence of a robust speedup. Both archived runs used the same hosted x86-64 runner family with 4-CPU affinity and synthetic cancellation fixtures. The study remains preliminary; representative application workloads, independent physical hardware and external numerical-method review remain outstanding. Scheduled-cycle audit 2026-11-27: PR #87 remains Draft on head 244761b6c44a2927345de4215b001bf909f8e662; exact-head quality CI 45883799154, 96-MiB memory-backed benchmark 45883799149 and actual CPU-thread workflow 45883799162 all succeeded. This is one hosted x86-64 runner family and a synthetic cancellation workload only; a second buffer size, representative workload and independent physical x86-64/ARM64 replication remain outstanding. Its base snapshot b97b30de is behind current main 8a69e6d9, so it needs refresh/revalidation before merge. Third hosted rerun (2026-11-27, Actions run 45897707859) was archived and independently reproduced in PR #94. Neumaier compensation-state merge was 48/48 correctly rounded in both runtimes; scalar Neumaier 42/48; naive 0/48. Free-threaded median speedup was 1.2589x versus matching serial Neumaier (worker medians 0.7733x/1.2125x/1.3546x/1.3090x for 1/2/4/8 workers), while GIL-enabled median was 0.7576x. CPU-time/wall-time exceeded 1.05 in 36/48 free-threaded runs and 0/48 GIL-enabled runs; native worker identity matched configured worker count in all 16 cases per runtime. Critical caveat: serial math.fsum remained 14.8–16.3x faster than the four-worker threaded Neumaier-state path on these fixtures. The two runtime modes used different hosted VM families, so cross-mode timing is confounded; this is not a general speedup claim. Run-19 independent reanalysis of PR #87's two raw 96-MiB KVM reports confirmed identical source SHA and host/cgroup settings; full Neumaier-state median speedup varied -12.2% to -17.5% across worker counts between runs. This is one virtualized x86-64 host and not physical replication or a general speedup claim. 2026-11-27 frozen native OpenMP timing audit: report says four effective CPUs (cpuset 0-3), but nine of 80 paired OpenMP process-CPU/wall samples exceed 4.05 across five cases; maximum 13.287713. This is a timing/provenance anomaly, not a proven code defect. Neumaier accuracy remains 40/40 and naive partials 0/40. The workload has input_storage_bytes=0 and is not a resident-array bandwidth test. Final schema-v2 hosted diagnostic run 45958399175: 80 samples (20 each at 1/2/4/8 workers), 0 worker/process cgroup mismatches, 0 unverified workers, process thread count matched the OpenMP team in all 80 runs. Known affinity/cpuset upper bound 4 CPUs; threshold 4.25; maximum process-CPU/wall ratio 4.004285619; 0/80 anomalies. One visible cgroup-v2 ancestor cpu.max file was unreadable, so exact effective capacity remains null. This does not reproduce the earlier 13.287713 anomaly or identify its cause; physical hardware replication remains outstanding. Cross-architecture replication 2026-11-27 (PR #124 head d2e5b14): native C/OpenMP accumulator tests ran on hosted Linux x86-64 and ARM64 (50 cases each, 5 repetitions). Full Neumaier state and exact superaccumulator were 40/40 correctly rounded on both architectures; naive partials and pairwise tree were 0/40. long double mantissa was 64 bits on x86-64 and 113 on ARM64; x86 long double passed 5/10 serial and 20/40 OpenMP cases, ARM64 passed 10/10 and 40/40. Exact superaccumulator best tested speedup was 1.50x/1.83x on x86-64 (8 workers, triplet/grouped) and 3.37x/3.34x on ARM64 (4/8 workers). Pairwise was faster but incorrect under strict rounding. ARM64 Python-thread replication (macOS/Ubuntu, GIL and free-threaded) had Neumaier-state 48/48 correct in each environment, scalar Neumaier 42/48 and naive 0/48. Free-threaded process CPU/wall reached 3.75x Ubuntu and 2.74x macOS, but median wall speedup for Neumaier-state remained below 1.0; this is CPU parallelism without net speedup on the tested small workload. tracemalloc median was ~25 KB GIL vs ~277 KB free-threaded, not RSS. Artifacts: native accumulator run 45961748438 (x86 15181375189 SHA f8eff09d..., ARM 15180639287 SHA 3d70bb9e...); native OpenMP 45961748471 (artifact 15180639238 SHA 82207369...); ARM64 threaded run 45961748435 (four artifacts 15180264380, 15180749225, 15180908527, 15181310576; ZIP SHA values in cross-architecture draft). Hosted-runner cross-replication only; physical-device and external independent replication remain outstanding.

The WMO roadmap article publishes aggregate findings, not the underlying country-by-country roadmap dataset; NOEMA cannot independently reanalyse the 35 roadmaps from this source alone.
The aggregate action-readiness contract is unpiloted; the minimum cell-size floor of 10 is a prototype default, not a guarantee of anonymisation or a substitute for local privacy review.

The UNDRR/WMO release provides published aggregates rather than the underlying country/activation-level records; NOEMA cannot independently verify reach, comprehension, protective action or avoided loss from this snapshot.
No authorized Georgian event-level warning/after-action data, representative last-mile survey, financing activation records or evacuation-specific exposed-population denominator is available.

streams.title: კვლევითი პლატფორმის სანდოობა, provenance და backup/restore
streams.problem: კვლევითი ჩანაწერების, job queue-ისა და audit trail-ის სანდოობა დამოკიდებულია მიკვლევადობაზე, უსაფრთხო backup-ზე და რეალურად შემოწმებულ restore-ზე; backup-ის წარმატებული შექმნა თავისთავად აღდგენადობას არ ადასტურებს.
streams.research_question: შეუძლია თუ არა NOEMA-ს local SQLite runtime-ს შექმნას თვითმყოფადი, integrity-შემოწმებული backup და უსაფრთხოდ აღადგინოს ის ისე, რომ WAL-only state, audit tampering ან არსებული database-ის overwrite არ მოხდეს?
streams.human_benefit: კვლევის ისტორიისა და სამუშაოების დაკარგვის რისკის შემცირება და შედეგების წარმომავლობის შენარჩუნება.
streams.hypothesis: SQLite file header-ის journal-version-ის პირდაპირი შემოწმება immutable read-only validation-თან ერთად სწორად უარყოფს WAL-mode backup-ს ისე, რომ source file არ შეიცვალოს.
methodology: SQLite official file-format და WAL documentation-ის მიხედვით file header-ის byte 18/19 შემოწმება
synthetic database backup/restore round-trip, WAL-mode negative case, tampered audit და no-overwrite regression tests
GitHub Actions-ის exact-head CI და mergeability verification
შემდგომ ეტაპზე encrypted off-host backup, retention/rotation და scheduled restore drills
On POSIX, stage each local SQLite snapshot in a fresh 0700 directory with a 0600 temporary database file; verify both permissions at the atomic no-overwrite publication boundary.

The restore-drill CLI requires an existing database, verifies it, creates an online SQLite snapshot and restores it into a second new path inside a temporary directory; it compares job/audit counts and the final audit-chain hash, confirms the backup bytes remain unchanged, and emits aggregate-only JSON without job IDs or payloads.
Define a strict JSON Schema 2020-12 metadata envelope for future off-host backups; tests enforce closed object boundaries and exclude secret/credential fields.
Validate proposed backup manifests with an executable JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 validator and strict format checking; keep cryptographic and provider checks explicitly out of scope.

Validate the strict manifest schema, then stream plaintext and ciphertext artifacts through SHA-256 and byte-length checks using one file descriptor; reject non-regular files, symlinks where O_NOFOLLOW exists, and obvious file mutation during hashing.

Runtime exact-byte Ed25519 detached-signature verification against caller-supplied trusted public keys, followed by streamed plaintext/ciphertext SHA-256 and byte-length checks; synthetic ephemeral-key tests only.

data_needs: synthetic SQLite databases with rollback-journal and WAL header states
backup/restore test fixtures and immutable source hash
CI job logs and exact commit SHA
Operator-approved non-production database for a real restore drill; record elapsed time and aggregate recovery evidence only.
risks: immutable=1 SQLite connection may mask the stored WAL journal mode
same-host backup does not protect against host/disk loss
backup is currently unencrypted and has no off-host retention automation
audit hash chain without signed external checkpoint does not prevent all tampering scenarios
Private staging-directory permissions are POSIX-specific; the final backup remains subject to the destination parent's ACL and can be exposed if that parent is too permissive.

The restore-drill CLI validates a same-host temporary filesystem round-trip only; it does not validate encrypted off-host storage, provider object versions, key recovery or clean-host disaster recovery.
A matching unsigned manifest and matching artifact hashes do not authenticate provenance; an attacker able to replace both files and the manifest can recompute the hashes.
A valid detached signature does not prove that a signed backup is the newest; rollback/freeze protection requires separately trusted monotonic state and freshness policy.
The local verifier authenticates exact manifest bytes only when the caller's public key is independently trusted; key compromise, revocation and rotation are not managed here.
blockers: No production backup encryption/decryption pipeline or off-host storage provider is configured.
Signing-key custody, rotation/revocation, threshold policy and independently trusted public-key provisioning remain unapproved and undeployed.

Rollback-resistant high-water state, immutable object-version/retention verification, clean-host restore, approved RPO/RTO and production ACLs remain unimplemented; no operator-approved deployed/staging database has been used.
streams.status_detail: Main contains local strict manifest/schema validation, streamed artifact digest/length checks and exact-byte Ed25519 verification using caller-supplied public keys. PR #85 is a separate draft architecture proposal for a provider-neutral linearizable compare-and-advance high-water authority and explicit restore lineage; its exact-head quality CI 45876372188 and CPU-thread workflow 45876372172 succeeded, but the PR is not merged and no service is deployed. Production anti-rollback, key custody, immutable object retention, off-host encryption and clean-host restore remain unimplemented. Scheduled-cycle audit 2026-11-27: PR #85 remains Draft at head 68e7385a798c19b807d75c3d41b27482ba0f402c; exact-head quality CI 45883729821 and actual CPU-thread workflow 45883729845 succeeded. The PR base a19252bb is behind current main 8a69e6d9. No external high-water service, production key custody, provider retention, encryption/decryption or clean-host restore is implemented; independent security review and trust-domain ownership remain blockers.
streams.next_step: Obtain independent security/architecture review and an owner for the separate trust domain and recovery path. Only then implement a provider-neutral CAS interface with deterministic concurrent-writer, stale-state, timeout and point-in-time restore tests; choose provider, RPO/RTO and retention with explicit owner approval. Do not create a Supabase project or reuse another project's database.
success_metrics: backup includes committed WAL data
restore rejects WAL-mode header and corrupted audit data before destination creation
restore never overwrites an existing destination and does not mutate source bytes
complete unit tests, frozen research reproductions, site build and publication-boundary checks pass
restore drill and encrypted off-host backup policy are documented and later independently tested
On POSIX, a test observes the staging directory at 0700 and the SQLite snapshot at 0600 immediately before no-overwrite publication, even when the destination parent is 0777.
restore-drill returns success only when source and restored databases are valid, job/audit counts and final audit hash match, and the backup bytes remain unchanged
restore-drill output contains aggregate metadata only and explicitly identifies the same-host-only evidence boundary
The future manifest is structurally validated against a strict schema; every object rejects unlisted fields and no secret/private-key material is permitted.
Runtime manifest validator accepts a synthetic schema-valid document and rejects malformed hashes, invalid UTC timestamps, missing fields and secret-like extra properties.
No claim of off-host disaster-recovery readiness until a clean-host restore is independently attested against approved RPO/RTO.

The verifier accepts only when both plaintext and ciphertext SHA-256 digests and byte lengths match the strict manifest; missing, modified, non-regular, symlink (where supported) and concurrently changing artifacts fail closed.
A synthetic manifest signature verifies only against an independently supplied trusted public key and exact manifest bytes; tampering, unknown signer and duplicate JSON keys fail closed.
Both local artifact hashes and byte lengths match the signed manifest before verification succeeds.
No claim of newest-backup or rollback protection until monotonic trusted state and freshness policy are independently persisted and tested.
No production disaster-recovery readiness claim until encrypted off-host artifacts are restored on a clean host against approved RPO/RTO.
